headline: Data center hardware start-up Oxide Computer has raised $445 million to make more of its pre-built server racks.
score_reason: Sizeable round for data center hardware, but demand claims come from the company's CEO.
importance_line: Shows demand for companies running cloud computing on their own premises rather than renting it, which matters to businesses weighing that choice; the demand and capacity claims come from Oxide's chief executive.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports that Oxide Computer, which sells a pre-built data center rack combining computing, storage and networking, raised $445 million in a Series D round led by Eclipse Capital, with AMD Ventures, Riot Ventures, Jane Street, Atreides Management and USIT also taking part. Chief executive Steve Tuck said Oxide has had to scale its manufacturing capacity 20 times over the past 12 months and that demand still exceeds supply.
notes: Investing.com page blocked (403); text read on SiliconANGLE, which reports the same round.
